extracted.intended_audience: conference program chairs, conference organizers, machine learning researchers, and peer-review researchers studying review quality
extracted.subtask_description: A report describing the design, implementation, and analysis of a randomized consistency experiment in the NeurIPS 2021 conference review process (10% duplicated papers reviewed by two independent committees) to quantify noise/arbitrariness in accept/reject decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — main claims reflect contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? [Yes]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the NeurIPS paper checklist applied to submissions; authors must affirm that abstract/introduction claims match actual contributions (Appendix A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — describe limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you describe the limitations of your work? [Yes] See Section 5.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to explicitly state limitations of their work in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — discuss potential negative societal impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss any potential negative societal impacts of your work? [Yes] See Section 5.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should address possible negative societal impacts and include this discussion in the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — read and conform to ethics review guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you read the ethics review guidelines and ensured that your paper conforms to them? [Yes]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure conformity with the venue's ethics guidelines and indicate so on the checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — state assumptions for theoretical results
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you state the full set of assumptions of all theoretical results? [N/A]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For papers with theoretical results, authors should state the full set of assumptions (if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — include complete proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you include complete proofs of all theoretical results? [N/A]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When theoretical claims are made, include the complete proofs (or point to supplemental material).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — include code/data/instructions for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you include the code, data, and instructions needed to reproduce the main experimental results (either in the supplemental material or as a URL)? [No]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to provide reproducibility artifacts where possible; in this study some data could not be released due to privacy. If applicable, include URL/supplement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — specify training details
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you specify all the training details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen)? [N/A]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When experiments are run, provide full training details to enable replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — report error bars
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you report error bars (e.g., with respect to the random seed after running experiments multiple times)? [Yes]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report uncertainty/variance where meaningful; the authors note that some plots lacked straightforward error bars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — report compute resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you include the total amount of compute and the type of resources used (e.g., type of GPUs, internal cluster, or cloud provider)? [No]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When experiments consume meaningful compute, report details of resources used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — cite existing assets
rubrics_metrics.description: If your work uses existing assets, did you cite the creators? [N/A]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using external code/data/models, cite creators and mention licenses where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — mention license of assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you mention the license of the assets? [N/A]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State licenses of reused assets when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — include new assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you include any new assets either in the supplemental material or as a URL? [N/A]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If new datasets/code are released, include them and their access details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — discuss consent and PII
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose data you’re using/curating? [Yes]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss consent and whether dataset contains personally identifiable information; the paper notes IRB and privacy constraints for the experiment data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — discuss offensive content / PII presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss whether the data you are using/curating contains personally identifiable information or offensive content? [Yes]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare presence of PII or offensive content and how it is handled (privacy protections, access restrictions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — include participant instructions/screenshots
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable? [Yes]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For human-subjects work, include full participant-facing materials and screenshots where relevant (appendices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — describe participant risks and IRB approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you describe any potential participant risks, with links to Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals, if applicable? [Yes]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document participant risks and IRB decision; this experiment had IRB review and restricted data access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist — report participant compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you include the estimated hourly wage paid to participants and the total amount spent on participant compensation? [Yes]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State compensation details or declare if participants were not compensated (program committee members were not compensated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form — Summary field
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary∗ Briefly summarize the paper and its contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should succinctly restate the paper's contributions to orient authors/ACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form — Main Review field
rubrics_metrics.description: Main Review∗ Provide a full review of the submission, including its originality, quality, clarity, and significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should address originality, technical quality, clarity, and significance; reviewer guidance URL provided for questions to address and formatting (Markdown/LaTeX).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form — Limitations And Societal Impact field
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations And Societal Impact∗ Have the authors adequately addressed the limitations and potential negative societal impact of their work? If not, please include constructive suggestions for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must evaluate whether authors addressed limitations and societal impacts and give constructive advice if not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form — Ethical Concerns field
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical Concerns: If there are ethical issues with this paper, please describe them and the extent to which they have been acknowledged or addressed by the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should explain ethical issues and how authors handled them; link to ethics guidelines is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form — Needs Ethics Review flag
rubrics_metrics.description: Needs Ethics Review∗ Should this paper be sent for ethics review? Options: Yes / No
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary flag used to route papers for additional ethics review; used in analyses of ethics-flag consistency between committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form — Ethics Review Area options
rubrics_metrics.description: If you flagged this paper for ethics review, what area of expertise would it be most useful for the ethics reviewer to have? (Options: Discrimination/Bias/Fairness; Inadequate Data and Algorithm Evaluation; Inappropriate Potential Applications & Impact; Privacy and Security; Legal Compliance; Research Integrity Issues; Responsible Research Practice; I don't know)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers selecting ethics review must indicate relevant expertise area(s) to route to appropriate ethics reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form — Time Spent Reviewing field
rubrics_metrics.description: Time Spent Reviewing∗ How much time did you spend reviewing this paper (in hours)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records reviewer effort; can be used to analyze workload and quality correlations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form — Rating (overall score) scale and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rating∗ Please provide an “overall score” for this submission. Options: 10: Top 5% of accepted NeurIPS papers, seminal paper; 9: Top 15% of accepted NeurIPS papers, strong accept; 8: Top 50% of accepted NeurIPS papers, clear accept; 7: Good paper, accept; 6: Marginally above the acceptance threshold; 5: Marginally below the acceptance threshold; 4: Ok but not good enough - rejection; 3: Clear rejection; 2: Strong rejection; 1: Trivial or wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should map overall evaluation to this 1–10 scale with the provided percentile/qualitative anchors for consistency across reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form — Confidence scale and descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidence∗ Please provide a “confidence score” for your assessment of this submission. Options: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment...; 4: You are confident...; 3: You are fairly confident...; 2: You are willing to defend your assessment, but it is quite likely that you did not understand central parts...; 1: Your assessment is an educated guess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers report how confident they are in their assessment (familiarity with area, care taken to check math/details) to inform AC weighting/interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form — Code of Conduct acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Code of Conduct∗ (Checkbox) While performing my duties as a reviewer (including writing reviews and participating in discussions), I have and will continue to abide by the NeurIPS code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must affirm adherence to the conference code of conduct when reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review form — Recommendation options
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation∗ Please recommend a decision for this submission. Options: Accept (Oral); Accept (Spotlight); Accept (Poster); Reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs must choose one of these discrete recommendation categories; these feed into program chair decisions and selection for oral/spotlight/poster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review form — AC Confidence / bump up/down options
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidence∗ Please qualify your recommendation. Options: You are absolutely certain; This decision can be bumped up (e.g., recommending accept as poster but would also make a fine spotlight); This decision can be bumped down (e.g., prefer accepting as poster but wouldn’t mind if it is rejected); You are not certain what the right decision should be. This is a submission you wish to discuss further with the SAC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs indicate certainty and whether their recommended tier is flexible; these fields were used in analysis to treat certain pairs (e.g., 'poster can be bumped down' vs 'reject') as consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review form — Metareview guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Metareview∗ Please provide a meta-review for this submission. Your meta-review should explain your decision to the authors. Your comments should augment the reviews, and explain how the reviews, author response, and discussion were used to arrive at your decision. If you want to make a decision that is not clearly supported by the reviews, perhaps because the reviewers did not come to a consensus, please justify your decision appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AC meta-reviews must explain rationale to authors and justify decisions inconsistent with reviewer consensus; used to communicate and justify outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review form — Review history disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Review History∗ Have you previously reviewed or area chaired (a version of) this work for another archival venue? (This information is only requested in order to collect aggregate statistics for NeurIPS 2021.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collects prior-review involvement for aggregate stats; not shared with authors or used to affect decision directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review form — Consider for award checkbox
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider For An Award (Checkbox) Yes, this paper should be seriously considered for an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs can flag papers for award consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance rule for duplicated papers (experiment-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Duplicated papers were accepted if at least one of the two copies was recommended for acceptance and no 'fatal flaw' was found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation detail of the consistency experiment: acceptance if any committee accepts unless the other finds an unfixable fatal flaw (e.g., error in major result). This rule increased conference acceptance rate by accepting some papers only because one committee favored them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment assignment isolation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When duplicating a paper, the two ACs were assigned to two different SACs so that no SAC handled both copies; newly invited reviewer for one copy was automatically added as a conflict for the other copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design choice to ensure independence between the two committees reviewing duplicated copies; also reused withdrawn abstract IDs to avoid revealing duplicates to committees, and committees were not told about experiment to avoid behavior change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response independence requirement (experiment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors were instructed to respond to each set of reviews independently; authors were notified right before initial reviews and asked to keep the experiment confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to avoid cross-influence between the two review threads; in practice, authors sometimes invested more effort in the copy they thought had higher chance.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC feedback categories for disagreement (qualitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three main categories for committee disagreement reported by ACs: (1) 'noise on the decision frontier' (borderline, no real disagreement); (2) genuine disagreements about value of contribution or severity of limitations; (3) one committee found a significant issue (close prior work, incorrect proofs, methodological flaws) that the other did not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to interpret causes of inconsistent recommendations when surveying ACs/SACs after experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bump up / bump down markers as decision-flexibility signals
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs could mark decisions as 'can be bumped up' or 'can be bumped down' to indicate flexibility in tier of acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis treated some combinations (e.g., 'poster accept that can be bumped down' + 'reject') as consistent, reducing measured inconsistency from 23.0% to 16.0%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metric — fraction of inconsistent accept/reject recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure: fraction of duplicated papers that were accepted by only one of the two committees (oral/spotlight/poster grouped as 'accept'). Observed: 203/882 = 23.0%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary consistency metric comparing committee-level recommendations; compared against random-baseline expectation for the same acceptance rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metric — random-baseline disagreement expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Baseline: expected fraction of inconsistent recommendations if acceptance decisions were made at random with the observed acceptance probability (e.g., for acceptance rate p, random disagreement = 2p(1-p)? — authors compute baseline values for comparison).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to contextualize observed disagreement; authors report relative improvements over this baseline (e.g., 35% improvement over random baseline at 22.7% acceptance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Metric — accept precision / arbitrariness (probability accepted->rejected)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept precision / 'arbitrariness': fraction (probability) of accepted papers that would be rejected if independently re-reviewed. Observed circa 50.6% (i.e., about half of accepted papers would be rejected by the other committee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors present this as complement to inconsistency and compare across acceptance thresholds; used to quantify how arbitrary accept decisions are.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metric — probability rejected->accepted on re-review
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure: probability that a randomly chosen rejected paper would have been accepted by the other committee if re-reviewed. Observed 14.9% in 2021 (17.5% in 2014).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symmetric measure to accept precision; provides sense of instability on reject side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metric — disagreement as function of acceptance threshold (selectivity sensitivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis: measure how disagreement and accept-precision change when varying acceptance threshold (e.g., accept only orals/spotlights vs. accept top x% by score). Observations: making conference more selective tends to increase arbitrariness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visualized in Figures 2 and 3 with random baseline curves and points showing actual and thresholded outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metric — ethics-flag overlap (consistency of ethics flags)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure: overlap in 'needs ethics review' flags between committees for duplicated papers; observed 23 flagged by one committee and 22 by the other with only 3 papers overlapping (~13%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to highlight high inconsistency/noise in which papers are sent for ethics review and uncertainty reviewers feel about flagging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metric — unanimity disagreement cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of duplicated papers where each committee was internally unanimous yet the two committees disagreed on accept/reject: 24 such papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates strong but conflicting community-level judgements across independent committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis consideration — author behavior confound
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may have responded differently to duplicated copies (e.g., spending more effort on the copy with higher scores), which can confound experiment outcomes (observed lower acceptance rate among duplicated papers than non-duplicated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimenters note this as limitation and compute acceptance rates/confidence intervals to quantify possible skew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental ethics / privacy rule for data access
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the data collected included personally identifiable information, only specified personnel (2021 program chairs, workflow manager, OpenReview staff) were permitted to access it; for accepted duplicated papers and opted-in rejected ones, both sets of reviews are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricts reproducibility of raw experiment data; authors explain why code/data for this experiment are not publicly released for privacy reasons.
